All:
# Thinking about all four seasons (winter, summer, spring, and fall), how
# do you rate the risk of the following hazardous weather events to you and
# the people in the area where you live? Lightning
#
# WxDash, the IPPRA Extreme Weather and Society Project. Rebuilds this
# chart from the released wave files and nothing else.
# Winter Weather (WW), WW21, WW22, WW23, WW24, WW25.

library(tidyverse)
library(srvyr)

# Read as character: a question asked in one wave is empty in the
# others, and a column empty for its first thousand rows is guessed
# logical, which turns every real value after it into NA.
ww21 <- read_csv("WW21_data_wtd.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
ww22 <- read_csv("WW22_data_wtd.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
ww23 <- read_csv("WW23_data_wtd.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
ww24 <- read_csv("WW24_data_wtd.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
ww25 <- read_csv("WW25_data_wtd.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

d <- bind_rows(
  ww21 |>
    transmute(
      PERSON_WEIGHT = as.numeric(PERSON_WEIGHT),
      resp = risk_lignt
    ),
  ww22 |>
    transmute(
      PERSON_WEIGHT = as.numeric(PERSON_WEIGHT),
      resp = risk_lignt
    ),
  ww23 |>
    transmute(
      PERSON_WEIGHT = as.numeric(PERSON_WEIGHT),
      resp = risk_lignt
    ),
  ww24 |>
    transmute(
      PERSON_WEIGHT = as.numeric(PERSON_WEIGHT),
      resp = risk_lignt
    ),
  ww25 |>
    transmute(
      PERSON_WEIGHT = as.numeric(PERSON_WEIGHT),
      resp = risk_lignt
    )
) |>
  filter(!is.na(resp), !is.na(PERSON_WEIGHT))

est <- d |>
  as_survey_design(ids = 1, weights = PERSON_WEIGHT) |>
  group_by(resp) |>
  summarise(p = survey_prop(proportion = TRUE, vartype = "ci"),
            .groups = "drop")

est <- est |>
  mutate(
    p = 100 * p, p_low = 100 * p_low, p_upp = 100 * p_upp,
    resp = factor(
      resp,
      levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
      labels = c("No risk", "Low risk", "Moderate risk", "High risk",
                 "Extreme risk")
    )
  )

ggplot(est, aes(x = p, y = fct_rev(resp))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = p_low, xmax = p_upp),
                width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = str_wrap(paste(
      "Thinking about all four seasons (winter, summer, spring,",
      "and fall), how do you rate the risk of the following",
      "hazardous weather events to you and the people in the area",
      "where you live? Lightning"
    ), 70),
    x = "Share of respondents (%)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# WxDash, the IPPRA Extreme Weather and Society Project. Rebuilds this
# chart from the released wave files and nothing else.
# Winter Weather (WW), WW21, WW22, WW23, WW24, WW25.
# Split by survey year (the `survey_year` column).

library(tidyverse)
library(srvyr)

# Read as character: a question asked in one wave is empty in the
# others, and a column empty for its first thousand rows is guessed
# logical, which turns every real value after it into NA.
ww21 <- read_csv("WW21_data_wtd.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
ww22 <- read_csv("WW22_data_wtd.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
ww23 <- read_csv("WW23_data_wtd.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
ww24 <- read_csv("WW24_data_wtd.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
ww25 <- read_csv("WW25_data_wtd.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

d <- bind_rows(
  ww21 |>
    transmute(
      PERSON_WEIGHT = as.numeric(PERSON_WEIGHT),
      survey_year = "2021",
      resp = risk_lignt
    ),
  ww22 |>
    transmute(
      PERSON_WEIGHT = as.numeric(PERSON_WEIGHT),
      survey_year = "2022",
      resp = risk_lignt
    ),
  ww23 |>
    transmute(
      PERSON_WEIGHT = as.numeric(PERSON_WEIGHT),
      survey_year = "2023",
      resp = risk_lignt
    ),
  ww24 |>
    transmute(
      PERSON_WEIGHT = as.numeric(PERSON_WEIGHT),
      survey_year = "2024",
      resp = risk_lignt
    ),
  ww25 |>
    transmute(
      PERSON_WEIGHT = as.numeric(PERSON_WEIGHT),
      survey_year = "2025",
      resp = risk_lignt
    )
) |>
  filter(!is.na(resp), !is.na(PERSON_WEIGHT))

est <- d |>
  as_survey_design(ids = 1, weights = PERSON_WEIGHT) |>
  group_by(survey_year, resp) |>
  summarise(p = survey_prop(proportion = TRUE, vartype = "ci"),
            .groups = "drop")

est <- est |>
  mutate(
    p = 100 * p, p_low = 100 * p_low, p_upp = 100 * p_upp,
    resp = factor(
      resp,
      levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
      labels = c("No risk", "Low risk", "Moderate risk", "High risk",
                 "Extreme risk")
    ),
    survey_year = factor(
      survey_year,
      levels = c("2021", "2022", "2023", "2024", "2025")
    )
  )

ggplot(est, aes(x = p, y = fct_rev(resp), fill = survey_year)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = p_low, xmax = p_upp),
                position = position_dodge2(reverse = TRUE),
                width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = str_wrap(paste(
      "Thinking about all four seasons (winter, summer, spring,",
      "and fall), how do you rate the risk of the following",
      "hazardous weather events to you and the people in the area",
      "where you live? Lightning"
    ), 70),
    x = "Share of respondents (%)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Survey year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
